There are, by your definition, no 0x01 "legacy" validators (yet). > 2) is that option available already? No. > 3) does 0x01 lock a validator to a particular EL address? Yes. If you want to change the address, you will have to do a full withdrawal + redeposit. is (3) the current response or the overall destination? meaning if you'd like a `0x01` post withdrawals being allowed, you'd have to withdraw/redeposit a pre Apr-2021 validator? in other words, are partial withdrawals not a solution that with current plans become available for pre April-2021 validators? As far as I know, the support for validators changing from 0x00 -> 0x01 credentials will come first (or along-with) partial/full withdrawal support. ( https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/issues/2758 ) oh okay, i now notice i misread your response to (3) thank you for the link where are withdrawals in the pipeline right now? (I'm sorry i haven't noticed it being spoken about on latest dev calls and it might be that i've missed the dev call where it was talked about) is it still realistic to expect a hard fork containing that within 6 months or more like 1+ year plus? (assuming a successful merge) 🤷‍♂️ You should know better than to ask questions about planning 😉 lol the truth... 🙂 Vaguely from what I understand is that everyone needs a little break after the merge, maybe discuss things async for a bit. And then in a month or so start dev calls again to see/slowly decide what goes in when that's already more than I knew, so thank you for that

excerpts.content: are most legacy validators `0x00` or `0x01`, if the former, how are validators going to be turned into `0x01` before partial withdrawals are enabled and does `0x01` lock them into a(n) particular EL address space?

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content:
> are most legacy validators 0x00 or 0x01,
legacy being.. what?

> how are validators going to be turned into 0x01
by sending a message to the network

> 0x01 lock them into a(n) particular EL address space
What is address space?

excerpts.author: schone_wizard
excerpts.content:
thank you for responding

1) validators created with the deposit-cli before the genesis of the CL
2) is that option available already?
3) does `0x01` lock a validator to a particular EL address?

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content:
> 1) validators created with the deposit-cli before the genesis of the CL
There isn't much/any difference between pre-genesis and post-genesis. 0x01 credentials became available in April 2021 I think, so quite a few months after. There are, by your definition, no 0x01 "legacy" validators (yet).

> 2) is that option available already?
No.

> 3) does 0x01 lock a validator to a particular EL address?
Yes. If you want to change the address, you will have to do a full withdrawal + redeposit.

excerpts.content: is (3) the current response or the overall destination? meaning if you'd like a `0x01` post withdrawals being allowed, you'd have to withdraw/redeposit a pre Apr-2021 validator?

excerpts.content: in other words, are partial withdrawals not a solution that with current plans become available for pre April-2021 validators?

excerpts.author: pietjepuk
excerpts.content: As far as I know, the support for validators changing from 0x00 -> 0x01 credentials will come first (or along-with) partial/full withdrawal support.
